scores.evidence: Money as integer minor units plus ISO currency. Prices are immutable and versioned. Corrections are credit notes, never edits.
scores.rationale: Ledger, idempotency, RLS, SAQ A and gapless numbering are described accurately, but webhook ordering and async payment states are not addressed and rounding stage is undefined.

scores.evidence: covers the plan catalog, subscriptions, usage metering, rating, a double-entry ledger, invoicing, tax, payment collection, dunning, entitlements, and ERP export
scores.rationale: Covers the core billing capabilities, with explicit deferrals and sensible assumptions, but dunning, trials, pauses and tax ID/reverse-charge handling are thin.

scores.evidence: Ledger, invoices, and payments are strongly consistent (single primary, serializable posting). Ingest favors availability
scores.rationale: Responsibilities and data ownership are clear and consistent across sections, with only a minor loose end (peak rate called UNKNOWN but also assumed 'low thousands').

scores.evidence: 4 h load at 3× peak ... with injected duplicates, reordering, late events, and consumer crashes
scores.rationale: Validations V0–V9 are tied to specific risks, run early before commitments, have checkable thresholds labeled as assumptions, and continue in production via invariant monitors, reconciliation and per-cohort gates.

scores.evidence: The plan proceeds on these assumptions; each one changes the plan if false
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labeled ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN/REQUIREMENT, with stated consequences if wrong and owners for confirmation.

scores.evidence: Anomaly circuit breaker: halt a run if its total deviates more than 20% from the previous cycle
scores.rationale: Double charges, duplicate or late usage, cross-tenant leaks, worker kills and cohort rollback are handled concretely, but disputes/chargebacks and out-of-order webhooks are missing.

scores.evidence: Terraform for infra. CI builds immutable images and runs forward-only migrations. One OpenTelemetry trace spans every tier
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, migrations, SLOs, on-call and restore drills are concrete and sized to one team, though incident response and access administration are brief.

scores.evidence: vendor fees over 3 years exceed build cost
scores.rationale: Cost drivers are named (vendor TCO, storage tiering, PSP/tax fees) and controls exist, but there are no run-cost estimates, Kafka/Postgres growth reasoning, or people-cost figures; the build-cost claim is deferred to V1.

scores.evidence: R3: once a number is issued it is permanent; EU VAT requires sequential numbering
scores.rationale: Every decision is tagged by reversibility with a revisit trigger, hard ones like invoice numbering, tenancy, IDs and PSP token custody get early validation, and adapter seams and exit paths are explicit.

scores.evidence: ≤ 3 deployables (ingest, billing core, workers) + Postgres + one stream, on the existing platform on-call rotation
scores.rationale: Starts from a modular monolith and defers ClickHouse, cells and sharding, but building a ledger and rating engine plus Kafka, Parquet and an 8-phase program with shadow billing is heavy.

scores.evidence: Depends on: V0; V1 (if V1 flips to buy, this phase shrinks to tenancy plus vendor integration and the plan is re-cut).
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered by stated dependencies, with a concrete first slice, specific tasks, checkable exit gates and explicit change-of-course conditions.

checklist.evidence: Money as integer minor units plus ISO currency.
Append-only double-entry ledger ... Corrections are credit notes, never edits.
Charge executor with idempotency key = invoice ID + attempt.
No card number (PAN) ever touches our systems; PSP-hosted fields only, so scope is SAQ A.
Postgres row-level security (RLS) enforced for the app role.
Dedupe and late-arrival window (design parameter: 72 h).
Subscription lifecycle: create, upgrade, downgrade, cancel, proration.
Gapless sequence per legal entity, allocated at finalization inside the ledger transaction (not at draft)
100% of ledger payment entries matched to PSP settlement daily; unmatched items resolved within 1 business day
entitlement cache on a billing outage → fail open with last-known state for tenants in good standing.
Buy the PSP (Stripe) and tax engine (Stripe Tax or Avalara). Build metering, rating, ledger, and invoicing

traps.evidence: Money as integer minor units plus ISO currency.
Corrections are credit notes, never edits.
No card number (PAN) ever touches our systems; PSP-hosted fields only
0 cross-tenant reads or writes over 100% of endpoints and jobs

note: Rigorous, well-validated, assumption-explicit plan with strong reversibility handling; it is thin on dunning/subscription/tax details, async payment states and cost quantification, and somewhat heavy in process.
